answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent network can enforce hardware enclave attestation at the dawn of each epoch. Each sparrow agent must run inside a certified secure processor, publishing cryptographic hardware measurements to an umber registry. An attacker incurs the verifiable cost of scarce physical silicon chips per identity, making virtualized duplication unprofitable. However, this relies on centralized chip vendors and remains susceptible to microarchitectural side-channel exploits.
